dedupe_keys.name: regional seismic loss and functional recovery of more than 15 000 woodframe residential buildings in los angeles

description: This case study assesses seismic loss and functional recovery for more than 15,000 residential woodframe buildings in the City of Los Angeles, to support the national effort to make functional recovery a code performance objective. It is published in Earthquake Engineering and Structural Dynamics (21 January 2025) by Laxman Dahal and Henry Burton of the University of California, Los Angeles, and Kuanshi Zhong of the University of Cincinnati. The authors propose a framework that uses automation, optimisation and distributed computing to run building-specific performance-based assessments across large inventories, and a stochastic event-set evaluation with site-specific ground motion selection for each building. Applied to Los Angeles, it reduced the runtime of the portfolio assessment from months to days. Coverage: over 15,000 woodframe residential buildings in Los Angeles. Access: journal article behind a subscription. Licence: Wiley terms; paid access. Caveats: one building type in one city; the abstract gives no loss figures. Simulation uses: regional earthquake risk and recovery modelling to appraise resilience-based design standards. Related records: the soft-story woodframe hybrid test data and the SimCenter tools.
name: Regional seismic loss and functional recovery of more than 15,000 woodframe residential buildings in Los Angeles
organisations: University of California, Los Angeles (Laxman Dahal, Henry Burton)
outcomes: An automated, distributed framework made a building-specific, event-set-based seismic loss and functional recovery assessment of more than 15,000 woodframe houses feasible, cutting runtime from months to days.
resources_used: Stochastic event set with site-specific ground motion selection
